frameworks: UK National Curriculum KS2 English Appendix 2

objectives.description: Use relative clauses beginning with who, which, where, when, whose, that, or an omitted relative pronoun
Use relative clauses with an omitted relative pronoun for concise, formal writing
Use modal verbs (might, should, will, must) to indicate degrees of possibility
Select modal verbs and adverbs (e.g. surely, perhaps) to indicate degrees of possibility appropriately for formal and informal contexts
Use fronted adverbials, and punctuate them with a comma
Use a wide range of fronted adverbials of manner, time, place and probability across a piece of writing for cohesion
Indicate parenthesis using brackets, dashes or commas
Choose between brackets, dashes and commas for parenthesis based on the level of formality and effect required
Use expanded noun phrases to convey complicated information concisely
Use expanded noun phrases with modifying adjectives, nouns and prepositional phrases for precision and economy
Use a range of prefixes (dis-, mis-, re-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, sub-, inter-, super-, anti-, auto-) to build new words
Use knowledge of prefixes (e.g. de-, over-, mis-, dis-, mis-) to understand and infer the meaning of unfamiliar words
Convert nouns/adjectives into verbs using suffixes (-ate, -ise, -ify), and add suffixes beginning with vowel letters to words ending in -fer
Use the suffixes -cious, -tious, -cial and -tial correctly, and use suffixes to distinguish word class (e.g. -ly, -ness, -ment, -ity)
Distinguish between homophones and other words that are often confused (e.g. affect/effect, principal/principle)
Distinguish between homophones and other words that are often confused in more formal/academic vocabulary (e.g. compliment/complement, stationary/stationery, ensure/insure)
Use a wide range of clause structures, varying position within the sentence for effect
Use a range of sentence structures to achieve particular effects, and identify simple, compound and complex sentences
Recognise vocabulary and structures appropriate for formal speech and writing, including the subjunctive
Use the perfect form of verbs to mark relationships of time and cause; use the present perfect vs past tense correctly
Use verb tenses consistently and correctly throughout a piece of writing, including the progressive and perfect forms
Use commas to clarify meaning or avoid ambiguity in writing
Use commas correctly in complex sentences to mark clause boundaries and resolve ambiguity
Use brackets and dashes to add extra information within a sentence
Use a single dash to mark the boundary between independent clauses
Link ideas across paragraphs using adverbials of time, place and number, and tense choices
Link ideas across paragraphs using a wider range of cohesive devices, including repetition of a word or phrase, grammatical connections and ellipsis

strands.name: Active & Passive Voice
strands.description: New for Y6: understanding how the passive voice changes the presentation and formality of information.

objectives.description: Recognise and use the passive voice to affect the presentation of information in a sentence

strands.name: The Subjunctive Form
strands.description: New for Y6: formal/subjunctive verb forms used in formal speech and writing.

objectives.description: Use the subjunctive form in formal writing and speech (e.g. 'If I were', 'The teacher requested that he hand in his book')

strands.name: Semicolons, Colons & Dashes for Lists
strands.description: New for Y6: punctuation to mark the boundary between independent clauses and to introduce lists.

objectives.description: Use a colon to introduce a list, and semicolons within a list
Use a semicolon to mark the boundary between independent clauses
Use hyphens to avoid ambiguity (e.g. 'man eating shark' vs 'man-eating shark')

strands.name: Synonyms & Antonyms
strands.description: New for Y6: precise vocabulary choices for effect.

objectives.description: Use a thesaurus-style knowledge of synonyms and antonyms to enhance vocabulary choices and avoid repetition

strands.name: Layout Devices & Bullet Points
strands.description: New for Y6: using layout to present information clearly in non-fiction writing.

objectives.description: Use bullet points consistently, and headings/sub-headings to structure non-fiction texts
